questions.question: Which coach received a royal knighthood in 2025 for contributions to national football?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gareth Southgate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gareth Southgate**, the head coach of the England national football team, received a royal knighthood in **2025** for his significant contributions to national football.
 
• Southgate has been instrumental in revitalizing the England football team, leading them to several major tournament successes, including reaching the **final of UEFA Euro 2020** and the semi-finals of the **2018 FIFA World Cup**.
 
• His leadership style, focused on creating a cohesive team culture and fostering young talent, has been widely praised and is considered a key factor in England's resurgence in international football.
 
• The knighthood is a recognition of his exemplary service to English football, including his efforts to promote sportsmanship and inspire a new generation of players.
 
• Gareth Southgate's achievements have not only elevated the performance of the national team but have also significantly enhanced the global reputation of English football.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gareth Southgate’s Career:**

 
 
• Born on **3 September 1970** in Watford, England, Southgate began his football career as a player, primarily playing as a defender for clubs like **Crystal Palace**, **Aston Villa**, and **Middlesbrough**.
 
• He earned **57 caps** for the England national team as a player and represented the country in major tournaments like the **1996 UEFA European Championship** and the **1998 FIFA World Cup**.
 
• After retiring as a player in 2006, Southgate transitioned into management and took charge of Middlesbrough as his first managerial assignment.
 
 
 
• **Achievements as England Manager:**
 
 
• He was appointed as the manager of the England national team in **2016**, initially on an interim basis, and was later confirmed as the permanent coach.
 
• Under his leadership, England reached the **2018 FIFA World Cup semi-finals**, their best performance in the tournament since 1990.
 
• In **2021**, Southgate guided England to the **UEFA Euro 2020 final**, where they narrowly lost to Italy in a penalty shootout.
 
• Southgate has been commended for creating an inclusive team environment, emphasizing mental health, and addressing social issues such as racism in football.
 
 
 
• **Knighthood and Honors:**
 
 
• Southgate’s knighthood in **2025** recognizes his contributions to sports, particularly his efforts to unite the nation through football.
 
• He was also awarded an **OBE (Order of the British Empire)** in **2019** for his services to football.
 
• His role as a leader extends beyond football, as he has been an advocate for youth development and sports education in England.
 
 
 
• **Other Noteworthy Coaches (Options):**
 
 
• **José Mourinho:** Known as "The Special One," Mourinho is a Portuguese coach with multiple UEFA Champions League titles but has not been knighted.
 
• **Pep Guardiola:** A Spanish coach celebrated for his tactical brilliance and numerous domestic league titles, especially with Manchester City, but also not knighted.
 
• **Roberto Martinez:** A Spanish coach who managed Belgium to the top of FIFA rankings but has not received a knighthood.

questions.question: What breakthrough innovation in renewable energy storage, which replaces liquid electrolyte with a solid one, was announced in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid-state sodium-ion battery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Solid-state sodium-ion battery** represents a breakthrough innovation in **renewable energy storage**, announced in **2025**.
 
• Unlike traditional batteries, it employs a **solid-state electrolyte** instead of liquid electrolytes, enhancing safety and reducing risks like leakage and fire hazards.
 
• Sodium-ion batteries rely on **sodium**, a more abundant and cost-effective element compared to lithium, making them suitable for large-scale energy storage applications.
 
• The solid-state design improves energy density and cycle life, ensuring longer battery performance while minimizing degradation over time.
 
• This innovation addresses key challenges in renewable energy integration, including the need for safer, more sustainable, and affordable battery solutions. 
 
• It is considered a major step forward in achieving global goals for **decarbonization** and transitioning to sustainable energy systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solid-state batteries:**

 
 
• They utilize solid electrolytes, such as **ceramics or polymers**, instead of liquid electrolytes found in conventional lithium-ion batteries.
 
• These batteries are known for their **high energy density**, longer life span, and enhanced safety features.
 
• Applications include **electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy storage**, and portable electronic devices.
 
 
 
• **Sodium-ion batteries:**
 
 
• Sodium-ion technology is gaining traction due to the **abundance of sodium**, which is cheaper and more sustainable compared to lithium.
 
• They are particularly suited for **grid-scale energy storage** to support renewable energy sources like solar and wind.
 
• Sodium-ion batteries are less prone to supply chain disruptions, as sodium is widely available across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with lithium-ion batteries:**
 
 
• Solid-state sodium-ion batteries are **less expensive** and safer due to the absence of flammable liquid electrolytes.
 
• While lithium-ion batteries have higher energy density, sodium-ion batteries offer a more sustainable solution for large-scale applications.
 
• Both technologies are pivotal in advancing energy storage systems to enable renewable energy adoption globally.
 
 
 
• **Global implications:**
 
 
• Solid-state sodium-ion batteries can significantly impact the **renewable energy sector** by providing affordable and scalable energy storage solutions.
 
• This innovation supports international efforts to combat **climate change** by reducing dependency on fossil fuels.
 
• Countries investing in this technology include **China, the United States, and Germany**, all aiming to lead in energy storage advancements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Benefits of solid-state sodium-ion batteries:**

 
 
• They reduce dependency on **rare earth materials** like lithium and cobalt, ensuring sustainability and cost-effectiveness.
 
• Their **solid electrolyte** eliminates risks associated with liquid electrolytes, such as leakage, corrosion, and thermal runaway.
 
• They are ideal for applications requiring **long-term energy storage** and high reliability.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Development costs and scalability remain key obstacles for solid-state sodium-ion batteries.
 
• Further research is needed to optimize **electrolyte materials** and manufacturing processes for widespread adoption.
 
 
 
• **Future prospects:**
 
 
• With advancements in material science and manufacturing, solid-state sodium-ion batteries are poised to revolutionize the energy storage industry.
 
• They hold the potential to accelerate the transition to **clean energy**, supporting global sustainability goals outlined by the **Paris Agreement**.

questions.question: Where was the 17th edition of the Nomadic Elephant defense joint military drill between India and Mongolia held in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **17th edition of the Nomadic Elephant defense joint military drill** between India and Mongolia was held in **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia**.
 
• This military exercise is a part of the annual defense cooperation program aimed at enhancing **military interoperability and building mutual trust** between the two nations.
 
• The exercise focuses on **counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations in mountainous terrains**, reflecting the geographical and strategic challenges faced by both nations.
 
• India and Mongolia share a strong defense partnership and cultural ties. The Nomadic Elephant drills are a testament to their **long-standing friendship and commitment** to regional peace and security.
 
• The drill often includes participation from **Indian Army personnel and Mongolian armed forces**, emphasizing joint operational capability and adaptability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India-Mongolia Defense Relations:**

 
 
• India and Mongolia established diplomatic relations in **1955**, and their defense partnership has grown significantly since then.
 
• Mongolia is strategically significant for India as it is a part of the **Act East Policy** and holds a pivotal position in Northeast Asia.
 
• Both nations have signed agreements on defense cooperation, including joint training programs and military drills.
 
 
 
• **Nomadic Elephant Military Exercise:**
 
 
• The Nomadic Elephant drills have been conducted annually for **over a decade**, showcasing the military collaboration between the two nations.
 
• The exercises focus on tactical maneuvers, humanitarian assistance, disaster relief, and counter-terrorism strategies.
 
• These drills provide an opportunity to exchange operational expertise and promote **regional security**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance of Ulaanbaatar:**
 
 
• Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, is known for its unique terrain comprising **mountains and plateaus**, providing an ideal environment for military drills.
 
• The city has hosted several international defense events, strengthening Mongolia’s role in global military cooperation.
 
 
 
• **India’s Defense Cooperation with Other Countries:**
 
 
• India actively participates in defense exercises with various countries, including the **Malabar Exercise** with Japan and the USA, and the **Indra Exercise** with Russia.
 
• Such initiatives help enhance military preparedness, promote peace, and strengthen strategic alliances globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mongolia’s Strategic Importance:**

 
 
• Mongolia acts as a buffer state between China and Russia, making it geopolitically significant in the region.
 
• India’s partnership with Mongolia strengthens its position in Northeast Asia and enhances diplomatic outreach.
 
 
 
• **International Military Exercises:**
 
 
• India participates in multiple military drills to foster bilateral and multilateral defense cooperation, such as **Yudh Abhyas** (with the USA) and **Sampriti** (with Bangladesh).
 
• These exercises contribute to capacity-building, strategic planning, and preparedness for global security challenges.
 
 
 
• **Defense Policy Objectives:**
 
 
• India’s defense policy focuses on promoting **regional peace**, enhancing security capabilities, and forming strategic alliances.
 
• Military drills like Nomadic Elephant are integral to achieving these objectives.

questions.question: How many people died due to natural disasters in 2024–25 as per provisional estimates from the Disaster Management (DM) division of the Home Affairs ministry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3080**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Disaster Management (DM) division** of the Ministry of Home Affairs is responsible for managing and reporting statistics related to natural disasters in India.
 
• As per the **provisional estimates** for the year **2024-25**, the total number of deaths caused by natural disasters is reported to be **3080**.
 
• The reported deaths include casualties due to various natural disasters such as **floods, cyclones, landslides, earthquakes, and extreme weather events**.
 
• Natural disasters disproportionately affect vulnerable populations, particularly those living in **disaster-prone areas** or with limited access to resources.
 
• The government has been working on enhancing **disaster preparedness, resilience, and mitigation strategies** to reduce the loss of lives and property caused by natural disasters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disaster Management Act, 2005:**

 
 
• The **Disaster Management Act** was enacted to provide a legal framework for the preparation and implementation of disaster management plans in India.
 
• It established the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** responsible for coordinating disaster response and mitigation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Types of Natural Disasters in India:**
 
 
• **Floods**: India experiences frequent floods due to heavy monsoons, particularly in states like Bihar, Assam, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• **Cyclones**: Coastal regions such as Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal are prone to cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **Landslides**: Mountainous regions like Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh experience landslides during heavy rains.
 
• **Earthquakes**: Seismic zones such as the Himalayan belt frequently experience earthquakes.
 
• **Heatwaves**: States like Rajasthan and Gujarat often face extreme heat conditions during summer months.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Disaster Management:**
 
 
• **National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP):** Aims to reduce vulnerability to cyclones and improve disaster response in coastal areas.
 
• **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF):** Established in various states to provide immediate assistance during disasters.
 
• **India's Meteorological Department (IMD):** Plays a key role in issuing **early warning systems** for extreme weather events.
 
 
 
• **Key Statistics and Reports:**
 
 
• **Global Climate Risk Index:** India ranks among the top countries most affected by climate-induced disasters.
 
• **UNDRR (United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction):** Highlights India’s efforts in improving disaster resilience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Natural Disasters:**

 
 
• Natural disasters cause significant damage to **infrastructure, livelihoods, and ecosystems**.
 
• They disproportionately impact **low-income groups** and marginalized communities.
 
• The loss of human lives, reported as **3080** in 2024-25, highlights the urgent need for enhanced **disaster risk reduction policies**.
 
 
 
• **Preparedness Measures:**
 
 
• Improved **forecasting technologies** and **early-warning systems** play a crucial role in mitigating disaster impacts.
 
• Community-based disaster management programs have proven effective in building **local resilience**.
 
 
 
• **International Support:**
 
 
• **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction:** India aligns its strategies with this global framework to enhance disaster resilience.
 
• **Global Climate Action:** Collaborative efforts to address climate change contribute to reducing disaster risks.

questions.question: In July 2025, Kavinder Gupta, who served as Deputy Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, assumed the office of Lieutenant Governor of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kavinder Gupta**, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader, served as the **Deputy Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir**. His political experience and administrative contributions have been noteworthy in the region.
 
• In **July 2025**, Kavinder Gupta assumed the office of **Lieutenant Governor (LG) of Ladakh**. Ladakh is a Union Territory (UT) in India, formed after the bifurcation of Jammu and Kashmir under the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019**.
 
• The position of Lieutenant Governor in Ladakh was created after the region was made a Union Territory in **October 2019**. The LG acts as the administrative head of the Union Territory.
 
• As the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, Kavinder Gupta's key responsibilities include overseeing the region's administration, ensuring the implementation of central government schemes, and addressing issues specific to Ladakh's development and governance.
 
• **Ladakh** is strategically significant for India, sharing borders with China and Pakistan. The Lieutenant Governor plays an essential role in maintaining security and fostering development in this sensitive region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Ladakh as a Union Territory:**

 
 
• Ladakh became a Union Territory on **31 October 2019**, following the abrogation of Article 370 of the Constitution of India.
 
• The **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019**, bifurcated the former state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
 
• Ladakh comprises two districts: **Leh** and **Kargil**.
 
• The Union Territory of Ladakh does not have a legislative assembly, and its governance is administered directly by the Lieutenant Governor.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Lieutenant Governor:**
 
 
• The Lieutenant Governor (LG) serves as the administrative head of a Union Territory.
 
• In Ladakh, the LG works closely with the central government to implement policies and maintain law and order.
 
• The LG is responsible for addressing local governance issues, ensuring development, and fostering harmony in the region.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Ladakh:**
 
 
• Ladakh shares borders with **China (Tibet Autonomous Region)** to the east and **Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan** to the west.
 
• It is a region of geopolitical significance due to its proximity to the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** and the **Line of Control (LoC).**
 
• Ladakh is also known for its unique geographical features, including the **Himalayas**, the **Karakoram Range**, and the **Indus River Basin**.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Cultural Aspects of Ladakh:**
 
 
• Ladakh's economy is primarily based on **tourism, agriculture, and animal husbandry**.
 
• The region is known for its unique **Buddhist culture**, monasteries, and festivals, which attract tourists globally.
 
• Efforts are being made to promote sustainable development, including solar energy projects and eco-tourism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019:**

 
 
• This act reorganized the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir (with a legislative assembly) and Ladakh (without a legislative assembly).
 
• The act was passed by the Parliament of India on **5 August 2019**.
 
 
 
• **First Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh:**
 
 
• **Radha Krishna Mathur** was the first Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, appointed on **31 October 2019**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Lieutenant Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The LG acts as a bridge between the central government and the Union Territory, ensuring effective implementation of policies and addressing the needs of the local population.

questions.question: Which of the following banks paid a record ₹8,076.84 crore dividend to the Government of India for FY25 in June 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI)**, India's largest public sector bank, paid a record dividend of **₹8,076.84 crore** to the **Government of India** for FY25 in **June 2025**. This dividend payment highlights the bank's robust financial performance.
 
• SBI's dividend payout is a direct result of its strong financial results, which include high profits and consistent growth in key banking metrics such as **Net Interest Income (NII)** and **Loan Growth**.
 
• The Government of India, as the majority shareholder in SBI, benefits from such dividend payments, which contribute to its revenue and fiscal budget.
 
• Dividends are distributed from the profits of the bank, reflecting its ability to generate substantial earnings and maintain liquidity while fulfilling regulatory requirements.
 
• SBI has consistently ranked as one of the top dividend-paying entities among public sector banks, showcasing its position as a leading financial institution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State Bank of India Overview:**

 
 
• Established in **1806** as the Bank of Calcutta, later renamed the State Bank of India in **1955**, it is headquartered in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra.
 
• It is India's **largest public sector bank**, offering a wide range of financial services including retail banking, corporate banking, treasury operations, and asset management.
 
• SBI operates a network of over **22,000 branches** and **62,000 ATMs** across India and has a presence in **36 countries worldwide**.
 
• The bank's market capitalization makes it one of the most valuable financial institutions in India.
 
 
 
• **Dividend Payment Process:**
 
 
• Dividends are paid from the profits earned by the bank, after fulfilling statutory reserves as mandated by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• The government, as the majority shareholder, receives the largest share of the dividend payout.
 
• Dividend payments are a reflection of the bank's profitability and financial health, and they contribute to the government's non-tax revenue.
 
 
 
• **Other Public Sector Banks:**
 
 
• **Indian Bank:** Headquartered in Chennai, established in **1907**. Known for its focus on retail banking.
 
• **Bank of India:** Founded in **1906**, headquartered in Mumbai, and provides services across India and abroad.
 
• **Bank of Baroda:** Established in **1908**, headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat, and is recognized for its global presence.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Dividend payments by public sector banks like SBI contribute to the government's revenue, aiding fiscal balance and budgetary allocations.
 
• These payments reflect the bank's efficiency in managing resources, profitability, and compliance with financial regulations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Ownership:**

 
 
• The Government of India holds a **57.49% stake** in SBI, making it the largest shareholder.
 
• Dividends paid by SBI contribute directly to the government's revenue stream, supporting various developmental initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Role of RBI:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** oversees the financial stability and compliance of banks, ensuring healthy dividend payouts.
 
• RBI mandates that banks must maintain adequate capital reserves before distributing dividends.
 
 
 
• **Recent Performance:**
 
 
• SBI reported a record net profit of ₹**50,232 crore** in FY25, showcasing its consistent growth and operational efficiency.
 
• The bank's **return on equity (ROE)** and **return on assets (ROA)** metrics further underline its robust financial performance.

questions.question: In July 2025, which Union Minister introduced the National Anti-Doping (Amendment) Bill 2025 in Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mansukh Mandaviya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mansukh Mandaviya**, the Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, introduced the **National Anti-Doping (Amendment) Bill, 2025** in the Lok Sabha in **July 2025**. This bill aims to strengthen the legal framework to combat doping in sports.
 
• The amendment aligns with international anti-doping standards set by the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** to ensure fairness and transparency in sports globally.
 
• The bill enhances the effectiveness of the **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)**, empowering it with greater autonomy and authority to take action against doping violations in Indian sports.
 
• It proposes stricter penalties for athletes and other personnel involved in doping violations, including suspension and fines, to deter such practices.
 
• The bill also includes provisions for **education and awareness** programs to inform athletes about the consequences of doping and promote ethical behavior in sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA):**

 
 
• Established in **2005**, NADA is responsible for promoting, coordinating, and monitoring anti-doping activities in India.
 
• Its primary functions include conducting **dope testing**, providing education and awareness to athletes, and implementing the anti-doping code in alignment with WADA guidelines.
 
• NADA works closely with sports federations, athletes, and support personnel to ensure compliance with anti-doping regulations.
 
 
 
• **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA):**
 
 
• WADA is an international organization established in **1999** to promote and coordinate the fight against doping in sports worldwide.
 
• It develops and enforces the **World Anti-Doping Code**, a set of rules and regulations for anti-doping efforts globally.
 
• WADA also accredits anti-doping laboratories, conducts research, and provides educational resources to combat doping.
 
 
 
• **Doping in Sports:**
 
 
• **Doping** refers to the use of prohibited substances or methods by athletes to enhance performance illegally.
 
• Common substances used for doping include **steroids, stimulants, and erythropoietin (EPO)**, which improve strength, endurance, and recovery.
 
• Consequences of doping include suspension, fines, disqualification, and damage to an athlete's reputation and career.
 
 
 
• **India’s Anti-Doping Efforts:**
 
 
• India has been actively working to combat doping through the efforts of NADA and collaboration with international organizations like WADA.
 
• Educational programs and workshops are conducted regularly to create awareness about anti-doping rules among athletes, coaches, and support staff.
 
• India has also increased the frequency of dope testing during national and international sports events to ensure fair play.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amendment Highlights:**

 
 
• The 2025 amendment introduces a **graded penalty system** to address the varying severity of doping violations.
 
• It ensures that athletes receive **fair hearings** and provides mechanisms for appeal in doping cases.
 
• Focus is given to **rehabilitation and reintegration** of athletes found guilty of doping, emphasizing education and counseling.
 
 
 
• **Global Ranking:**
 
 
• India has historically faced challenges in doping, often ranking among the top countries with doping cases in reports by WADA.
 
• Efforts like this amendment aim to improve India’s international reputation in sports and ensure a level playing field for athletes.
 
 
 
• **Way Forward:**
 
 
• Stronger collaboration between NADA, sports federations, and athletes is essential for effective implementation of anti-doping measures.
 
• Increased investment in **research and development** of testing methods will help in detecting newer substances and methods of doping.
 
• Public awareness campaigns can further promote ethical practices in sports and discourage doping at all levels.

questions.question: The Military Combat Parachute System (MCPS), which successfully carried out a combat freefall jump from 32,000 feet in October 2025, was indigenously created by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Military Combat Parachute System (MCPS)** was developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**, a premier agency under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India.
 
• MCPS successfully carried out a **combat freefall jump** from an altitude of **32,000 feet** in **October 2025**.
 
• This parachute system is **indigenously created**, showcasing India's technological advancement in defense systems and its ability to meet critical military requirements.
 
• The **MCPS** is designed for high-altitude operations, enabling soldiers to execute missions in adverse environments with precision and safety.
 
• The development of such systems by DRDO highlights India's commitment to **self-reliance** under the **Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative**, focusing on indigenous production of advanced defense equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**

 
 
• DRDO was established in **1958** and is headquartered in **New Delhi, India**.
 
• The organization develops cutting-edge defense technologies and systems, ranging from missiles, combat vehicles, radars, and electronic warfare systems to advanced parachutes.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Defence and has over **50 laboratories** dedicated to various research areas.
 
• Some of DRDO's notable achievements include the **Agni missile series**, **BrahMos missile**, and **Tejas fighter jet**.
 
 
 
• **High-Altitude Parachute Systems:**
 
 
• Parachutes designed for high-altitude operations enable **combat personnel** to perform missions under extreme conditions such as low oxygen levels and sub-zero temperatures.
 
• Such systems incorporate **advanced materials** to ensure durability, lightweight construction, and precision deployment.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Defense Manufacturing:**
 
 
• India's focus on **self-reliance** in defense manufacturing is part of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative**, aiming to reduce dependency on foreign suppliers.
 
• Organizations like DRDO, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), and Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) play a critical role in achieving this goal.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Military Combat Parachutes:**
 
 
• Used for **special operations**, reconnaissance, and infiltration missions in enemy territories.
 
• Enables deployment in **mountainous terrains**, deserts, and other challenging environments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DRDO's Role in National Security:**

questions.question: Which of the following is the unified inundation forecasting system launched by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in July 2025 that provides two‑days advance inundation forecasts up to village level in the form of flood‑inundation maps and water‑level predictions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C‑FLOOD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **C‑FLOOD** is a unified inundation forecasting system launched by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** in **July 2025**.
 
• The system provides **two-day advance flood inundation forecasts** at the village level, allowing for better preparedness and disaster management.
 
• It generates **flood-inundation maps** and **water-level predictions**, which are critical for local authorities and communities to plan evacuation and relief operations.
 
• The initiative is part of the government's focus on leveraging **technology and data analytics** to mitigate the impact of floods, which annually affect millions across India.
 
• This forecasting system integrates data from multiple sources, including weather forecasts, hydrological models, and satellite imagery, to provide accurate and actionable insights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Flood Forecasting:**

 
 
• Flooding affects over **75 lakh hectares** of land annually in India, causing significant economic losses and affecting livelihoods.
 
• Forecasting systems like C‑FLOOD reduce the loss of life and property by enabling timely evacuation and resource allocation.
 
 
 
• **Technology Used in C‑FLOOD:**
 
 
• Incorporates **hydrological and hydraulic models** to simulate flood scenarios.
 
• Utilizes **satellite data** for real-time monitoring of water levels and rainfall patterns.
 
• Relies on **machine learning algorithms** to improve the accuracy of predictions over time.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti's Role:**
 
 
• The Ministry oversees water resource management, including flood control and forecasting.
 
• It collaborates with agencies such as the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and **Central Water Commission (CWC)** for data sharing and analysis.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Systems:**
 
 
• Unlike older systems, C‑FLOOD provides **granular, village-level data**, making it more effective for localized disaster management.
 
• It offers forecasts up to **48 hours in advance**, which is a significant improvement over earlier models that provided shorter lead times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Flood Forecasting:**

 
 
• Limited availability of high-resolution data in remote areas.
 
• Need for inter-agency coordination to ensure timely dissemination of forecasts.
 
• Improving community awareness and response mechanisms to maximize the utility of forecasts.
 
 
 
• **Other Flood Management Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• The **National Flood Forecasting and Warning Network** run by the Central Water Commission.
 
• Deployment of **Automatic Rain Gauges (ARGs)** and **Telemetry Systems** for real-time data collection.
 
• State-level initiatives such as flood zoning and embankment construction.

questions.question: Which of the following was designated as the 58th Tiger Reserve of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhav National Park**__.

__
 
• **Madhav National Park** was designated as the **58th Tiger Reserve of India** in 2023, under the Project Tiger initiative, which aims to conserve tigers and their habitats.
 
• Madhav National Park is located in the **Shivpuri District of Madhya Pradesh**, a state known for its significant contribution to tiger conservation in India.
 
• This designation is part of the Indian government’s effort to expand the network of protected areas for tigers and strengthen biodiversity conservation.
 
• The park spans over an area of approximately **354 square kilometers**, making it an ideal habitat for tigers and other wildlife species.
 
• The inclusion of Madhav National Park as a tiger reserve reflects the government’s commitment to achieving conservation goals under the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Madhav National Park:**

 
 
• Madhav National Park was established in **1959** and is one of the oldest national parks in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is named after **Madhav Rao Scindia**, a prominent figure from the royal family of Gwalior.
 
• The park is home to a variety of wildlife, including **Tigers, Leopards, Indian Gazelle (Chinkara), and Nilgai**.
 
• It also features two important water bodies, **Sakhya Sagar Lake** and **Chandrashila Lake**, which provide water resources for the animals and act as tourist attractions.
 
• The park’s vegetation is primarily dry deciduous forest, interspersed with grasslands, creating an ideal environment for predators and prey.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched in **1973**, Project Tiger is a flagship conservation initiative of the Government of India, aiming to protect tigers and their natural habitats.
 
• The project is implemented by the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** and has led to the establishment of **tiger reserves** across the country.
 
• India is home to approximately **70% of the global tiger population**, and the project has been pivotal in increasing tiger numbers through scientific management and anti-poaching measures.
 
• The latest All-India Tiger Estimation Report of **2022** recorded a significant increase in tiger population, emphasizing the success of such initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Reserves in Madhya Pradesh:**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is known as the **"Tiger State of India"** due to its high tiger population and the presence of multiple tiger reserves.
 
• Notable reserves include **Kanha Tiger Reserve, Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve, Panna Tiger Reserve, Satpura Tiger Reserve**, and now **Madhav National Park**.
 
• The state’s tiger reserves contribute significantly to eco-tourism and conservation education.
 
 
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):**
 
 
• The NTCA was established in **2006** under the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 to strengthen tiger conservation efforts in India.
 
• It provides funding, technical support, and policy guidance for tiger reserves and ensures adherence to conservation protocols.
 
• The authority also conducts periodic assessments of tiger populations and their habitats.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh** has consistently ranked among the top states in India for tiger conservation efforts, earning national and international recognition.
 
• The designation of Madhav National Park as the **58th Tiger Reserve** aligns with the objectives of the **Global Tiger Initiative**, a worldwide effort to double tiger populations by 2022.
 
• The park’s location near urban centers like Gwalior and Shivpuri increases its potential for eco-tourism and awareness programs.
 
• The involvement of local communities in conservation activities under the NTCA framework ensures sustainable management and reduces human-wildlife conflict.
 
• Continuous monitoring and capacity-building initiatives are crucial for the long-term success of tiger reserves like Madhav National Park.
